body:
Split out of #931 (Zom 100 grabbed *The Convert*). This is the part that needs a design decision; #931 itself is fixed.

## The problem
Some indexers (mostly NinjaCentral, also DrunkenSlug) tag another movie's releases with a library movie's TMDB/IMDb id. Radarr trusts the id, so its own search (on add, Force Search, any MoviesSearch) approves and grabs the wrong movie. Radarr never imports it on its own: the finished download blocks with "matched to movie by ID" (or "Movie [X] was not found in the grabbed release"), and since PLAN-077 P2 the janitor's Import Check classes it `title_mismatch` (report only). The cost is a missing movie whose slot is held by a wrong download until someone removes it, and a wasted download (often a 15 to 25 GB UHD or remux).

## Evidence (read-only census, 2026-10-13)
Radarr history since 2026-07-03 (1362 grabs, all 9386 movies): `movieTitleEvidence` called 27 movies' grabs `ambiguous`.
- **8 were another movie:** Zom 100 (2023) <- *The Convert* 2023; Croc (2007) <- *Supergator* 2007; A Movie of Eggs (2006) <- *Alatriste* 2006; Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion (2014) <- Star Wars Rebels season packs (4 grabs, July to September); Hannibal Rising <- *Dead Silence*; Horrible Bosses 2 <- *Chef*; Scooby-Doo (2002) <- *Spy Kids 2*; probably Josee, the Tiger and the Fish <- the Korean *Josee* (2020). The first four were missing movies held for days to weeks; staff removed the downloads by hand in batches.
- **19 were the same film** under another title, year or spelling: *Vaiana* for Moana, *Hopeu* (the romanized Korean title) for Hope (2026), *Pokemon 2 The Power of One*, *Terrifier 2016*, *Dead Man s Wire 2025*, German titles, and others. So a name verdict alone is not a safe trigger for an automatic removal (this is also why `title_mismatch` stays report only: PLAN-065 ladder log, 2026-10-13).

## Options
1. **Leave it (recommended for now).** The Release Pick refuses these rows (DESIGN-055 P5 decision 15), staff or a person picks a real release, and `title_mismatch` reports the stuck download. About one wrong-movie grab every two weeks.
2. **A Radarr per-movie Mislabel Block.** One app-owned tag on each affected movie plus a tag-scoped release profile whose "must not contain" terms name the other movie (e.g. `The.Convert.2023`), written only by staff from evidence. Release names carry nothing of the movie they were tagged for, so the block cannot be scoped by text the way the Sonarr Mislabel Block is: it needs tags. That is a new write kind (movie tags), so it needs an ADR line (CLAUDE.md hard rule 4) amending ADR-110 C-04 / ADR-113. Estimate: a writer with read-back and expiry, a migration, a staff CLI, tests; about the size of the Sonarr block.
3. **A narrowed janitor enforce cell** for Radarr `title_mismatch` when Radarr's own rejection names a different library movie. Amends ADR-110 C-02 (no enforce cell). It clears the slot but does not stop the next search grabbing another posting of the same wrong movie.

**Recommendation:** option 1 now. Revisit option 2 if the `title_mismatch` census shows Radarr wrong-movie grabs more than about twice a month, or a missing movie stays held by one for more than a week.

## Already done in #931
- Zom 100: staff Release Pick of `Zom.100.Bucket.List.of.the.Dead.2023.1080p.NF.WEB-DL.DDP5.1.Atmos.x264-OzONE`, imported 2026-10-13 14:45Z (Radarr movie 9830; Plex HaynesTower and PlexOps show the 130-minute film).
- Croc: staff override pick of `Croc.2007.720p.WEB.x264-ASSOCiATE` (the only real releases are 720p or below), imported 14:41Z.
- A Movie of Eggs and Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion: the indexers have no real release; every listed one is the wrong title (all blocklisted or below the profile), so Radarr cannot grab them again on its own.
- Reporting the bad tags to NinjaCentral: skipped. Its per-release report needs a signed-in browser session; there is no API or other obvious channel from the cluster.
title: Radarr: refuse id-mistagged wrong-movie releases at grab time (needs a design decision)
